newsitem.title: UK: Russian finance minister says budget deal possible.
newsitem.headline: Russian finance minister says budget deal possible.

text.p: Russian Finance Minister Alexander Livshits said on Friday that the country's communist dominated parliament or Duma may agree a 1997 budget before the end of the year.

Russia's budget debate has been mired over disagreements on social spending and tax collection and the latter caused the International Monetary Fund to suspend payments of a $10.2 billion loan to the country.
This has imperilled the country's finances as many state workers have not been paid and the country's infrastruture is crumbling.
"There is still a possibility that the budget for 1997 will be approved this year," Livshits told a press conference in London.
Representatives of the Duma, the Federation Council upper house of parliament and the government agreed a draft budget by a razor thin margin in a reconciliation commission on Wednesday.
But deputies said this did not mean the budget would be approved when the Duma, dominated by the communist opposition, begins debating it on November 22.

"If there were no credits from the IMF we would face problems financing the budget in 1996. In any case, we do expect to receive the $1 billion due from the IMF by the end of 1996," said Livshits' deputy Mikhail Kasyanov.

Russian tax revenues improved sharply last month and officials highlighted this in interviews and press comments before the IMF's latest monitoring mission arrived. The mission is likely to be in Moscow until late next week.

The government, which has set up an emergency commission to force tax debtors to pay, blames companies who do not pay their bills. The firms say they cannot pay because their clients -- including the government and the state sector -- owe them cash.
Livshits was in London to drum up interest in Russia's planned eurobond issue of up to $500 million.
